title: Trigraphs
keyIdea: A trigraph is three letters that make one sound. igh says the sound in night, air in chair, ear in hear, and are in square. When you count the sounds in a word, the three letters of a trigraph count as one: night has five letters but three sounds, n, igh, t. ear can make two sounds: ear as in hear and near, or air as in bear and pear. air and are can make the same sound, so learn which one each word uses: chair, but care.
familyTip: Hunt for trigraphs at bedtime. Say night, light, right and bright, and ask your child to hold up one finger for each sound: n, igh, t is three fingers, not five. Write the words on paper and colour igh in one colour so the three letters stay together. Then play 'hear or bear?': say near, pear, year and wear and sort them into two piles by the sound ear makes.

visual.caption: Which 3-letter team is in the word? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

bins: air or are, as in chair

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag a 3-letter team into a picture word, count sounds not letters, find the trigraph, sort the two sounds of ear, and mend split spellings.

kid: Some sounds need three letters. Look at night. The letters i, g and h work as a team. Together they say igh. Three letters that make one sound are called a trigraph.
Here are four trigraphs. igh is in night. air is in chair. ear is in hear. are is in square.
To count the sounds in a word, say it slowly. Hold up one finger for each sound. Night is n, igh, t. That is three sounds, but five letters. The team gets one finger.
Watch out! ear can say two sounds. In hear and near it says ear. In bear and pear it says air. And air and are can sound the same. Chair uses air. Care uses are.
adult: Ages 5 to 6. The National Curriculum in England (English Appendix 1, Year 1) lists the trigraphs igh (high, night, light, bright, right), air (fair, pair, hair, chair), ear (dear, hear, near, year), ear with the air sound (bear, pear, wear) and are (bare, care, share, scared) among the graphemes children should read and spell. Letters and Sounds teaches igh, ear, air and ure as Phase 3 trigraphs. Key terms: phoneme (a sound), grapheme (the letters that write it), digraph (two letters, one sound), trigraph (three letters, one sound), segmenting and blending.

The idea that matters most is one-to-one: one phoneme, one grapheme. In night the grapheme igh writes one phoneme, so a child segments n, igh, t and blends those three back into the word. When counting, a trigraph gets one tap or one finger, just like a single letter or a digraph such as ch.

Common mistakes: sounding every letter, so night becomes n-i-g-h-t; counting letters instead of sounds; splitting the trigraph wrongly, as in reading the ch and then hai in chair; spelling by sound alone, as in nite, brite, heer and chare; and thinking ear always says the same sound, so bear is read to rhyme with hear. Be careful too with air and are, which make the same sound; there is no safe rule at this age, so learn the common words in sets.

In the lab your child drags igh, air, ear or are into a picture word (night, chair, light, hear, square), counts the sounds in five words by tapping a number, taps all three letters of the trigraph in five words, sorts six ear words into 'like hear' or 'like bear', and mends four sentences with a spelling slip. Every wrong move names the slip, for example '5 is how many letters'.

practice.prompt: Which 3 letters make 1 sound in light?
practice.hint: Say light slowly: l, then the middle sound, then t.
practice.explain: igh is the trigraph. light is l, igh, t: three sounds.

practice.prompt: Mia reads {n} words. Each word has one trigraph, like igh in night. How many trigraphs does she read?
practice.explain: One trigraph in each word, so {n} words have {n} trigraphs.

practice.prompt: How many sounds are in chair?
practice.hint: ch is one sound. air is one sound.
practice.explain: chair is ch, air: two sounds, even though it has five letters.

practice.prompt: A word has {n} letters. Three of them are a trigraph. Every other letter makes its own sound. How many sounds does the word have?
practice.hint: The 3 letters of the trigraph count as just 1 sound.
practice.explain: Three letters become one sound, so {n} letters make {=n-2} sounds.

practice.prompt: In which word does ear sound like air?
practice.explain: pear rhymes with chair, so its ear says air. near and dear say ear.

pool.hint: The middle sound is igh, three letters.
pool.explain: bright is b, r, igh, t. igh needs all three letters.

pool.hint: Think of igh in night: how many letters, and how many sounds?
pool.explain: A trigraph is three letters that make one sound, like igh, air and ear.

pool.prompt: How many sounds are in high?
pool.hint: Say it: h, then the igh sound.
pool.explain: high is h, igh: two sounds from four letters.

pool.prompt: Which word has ear like in hear?
pool.explain: year rhymes with hear. In bear and wear, ear sounds like air.

pool.prompt: Ben writes {n} words with air, like hair. He colours each air team. How many teams does he colour?
pool.hint: Each word has one air team.
pool.explain: One air team in each word, so {n} words give {n} teams to colour.

pool.prompt: Which word uses are for the air sound?
pool.hint: Look for the letters a, r, e.
pool.explain: share uses are. hair and fair make the same sound but use air.

pool.prompt: There are {n} cards with igh words. Zoe reads {k} of them. How many are left to read?
pool.hint: Take the cards she read away from all the cards.
pool.explain: {n} cards take away {k} read leaves {=n-k} cards.

pool.hint: The sound is ear. Which three letters write it?
pool.explain: hear uses the trigraph ear: h, ear.

pool.prompt: How many sounds are in night?
pool.hint: Hold up a finger for each sound. igh is one finger.
pool.explain: night is n, igh, t: three sounds from five letters.
